item.title: Sqwod Daily · Thursday, 29 October 2026
item.description: Intake Breathing closes a $62M round for its magnetic nasal dilator, while Garmin posts record fitness revenue and an Indiana club triples recovery service usage.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 29 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Thursday, 29 October 2026 · Weekday
Intake Breathing raises $62M for nasal dilator, Garmin fitness revenue hits $694M & Ozwell triples recovery usage
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Intake Breathing closes a $62M round for its magnetic nasal dilator, while Garmin posts record fitness revenue and an Indiana club triples recovery service usage.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Intake Breathing
 $62M
funded by Camino Partners to expand magnetic nasal dilator into mainstream retail
 
Connect the dots
Intake Breathing lands $62M to push magnetic nasal dilator into retail
Jim Castillo, a medical device engineer, invented a reusable magnetic band and adhesive tab system that mechanically opens the nasal valve to improve airflow. His son-in-law Alex Hauck runs the company as CEO. Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, has put $62 million into Intake Breathing, marking the brand's first significant outside capital. The funding will take the family-run business into mainstream retail.
For coaches and studio owners building recovery or sleep programming, the raise signals that breathing and recovery products are attracting serious consumer brand investment. As Intake moves into retail, members will encounter the brand outside the gym, which gives coaches an opening to address nasal breathing and airflow as part of their recovery conversations.
 
The rundown
01
$62M Backs Intake Breathing's Magnetic Nasal Strip Expansion
Intake Breathing has raised $62 million from Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, to grow its magnetic nasal dilator brand into mainstream retail. Intake, founded by medical device engineer Jim Castillo and run by CEO Alex Hauck, makes a reusable magnetic band and adhesive tab system that mechanically opens the nasal valve to improve airflow, unlike traditional adhesive strips. The raise signals that sleep, recovery and breathing performance products are attracting serious consumer brand investment, a category relevant to studios and coaches building recovery or sleep programming.
Source: Athletech News →
02
Garmin fitness revenue rises 16% to $694m in Q3 2026
Garmin reported third-quarter fitness segment revenue of $694 million, up 16% year over year, for the quarter ended September 26, 2026, with operating income of $231 million and a 33% operating margin. In July, the company launched the Cirqa Smart Band, a screenless wearable priced at $199.99 with no subscription fee, targeting the same recovery and wellness tracking market as Whoop. For studio and gym operators evaluating wearable partnerships or member-facing technology, Garmin's subscription-free model is a direct contrast to Whoop's paid membership structure and may influence member purchasing decisions.
Source: Athletech News →
03
Ozwell Fitness tripled recovery service usage after consolidating wellness under one roof
Gemi Ozdemir opened Ozwell Fitness in Carmel, Indiana, combining red light therapy, personal training, sauna and other recovery services in a single facility, using Neo Science wellness technology. The club attracted thousands of new members and tripled usage rates for some recovery services, with Ozdemir reporting strong retention. For operators, the results suggest that bundling recovery and training in one location can drive both engagement and member loyalty.
Source: Athletech News →
04
Lawler and Diaper: value, innovation and human connection drive operator success
Total Fitness CEO Sophie Lawler and Fitness First CEO Marc Diaper told the HCM Summit that delivering value, investing in innovation and protecting human connection are central to fitness operators' success. The two chief executives spoke at the event, according to Health Club Management.
Source: Health Club Management →
 
Stat
$694 million
Garmin fitness segment revenue for the quarter ended September 26, 2026
Garmin's fitness segment, its largest by revenue, grew 16% year over year with a 33% operating margin, and its new $199.99 screenless Cirqa Smart Band carries no subscription fee, a direct contrast to Whoop's paid membership model that may shape how members choose wearables.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Wednesday, 28 October 2026
item.description: SATS posted a 22% EBITDA rise in Q3 by lifting revenue per member across fewer clubs, while the DSSV shifts its 2026 event to Spain and Oura expands into India.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 28 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Wednesday, 28 October 2026 · Weekday
SATS Q3 EBITDA up 22% on higher revenue per member, DSSV event moves to Málaga & Oura Ring 5 launches in India
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
SATS posted a 22% EBITDA rise in Q3 by lifting revenue per member across fewer clubs, while the DSSV shifts its 2026 event to Spain and Oura expands into India.
Sqwod
 
The rundown
01
DSSV annual fitness industry event moves to Málaga for October 2026
The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, will hold its 2026 annual event at the Hotel Meliá Costa del Sol in Torremolinos, near Málaga, Spain, from 20 to 23 October 2026. Tickets are priced at €720 per participant, and the programme includes expert talks, networking, and Les Mills workouts, with the opening reception hosted by DSSV chairman Prof. Dr. Thomas Wessinghage on 20 October. This is the first time the event leaves Mallorca, where the two previous editions were held.
Source: DSSV →
02
SATS Q3 EBITDA rises 22% as group exercise and revenue per member climb
Nordic fitness operator SATS reported a 22 percent increase in third-quarter EBITDA before IFRS 16 (a lease-accounting standard that affects how costs are reported) driven by higher revenue per member and growth in group exercise, across a smaller number of clubs. The results show that reducing club count while lifting revenue per member can expand earnings, a signal for operators weighing portfolio size against member yield.
Source: Health Club Management →
03
Fit & Fabulous Somerset raises nearly £500 for Breast Cancer Now
Burnham-on-Sea and Highbridge fitness group Fit & Fabulous Somerset raised nearly £500 for Breast Cancer Now by running pink-themed classes as part of the charity's Wear It Pink campaign. Owner Charlotte Simmons said the total is still growing. The campaign shows how small studios can use charity tie-ins to drive class attendance and community engagement without major cost.
Source: Burnham-On-Sea.com →
04
Oura Ring 5 launches in India from Rs 39,900 with AI blood pressure feature
Oura launched its Ring 5 in India on October 22, 2026, priced from Rs 39,900 to Rs 50,900 depending on finish, with pre-orders on Amazon and Croma. The device is 40% smaller by volume than the Ring 4, carries 12 signal pathways, offers up to nine days of battery life, and includes Health Radar, an AI feature that monitors nighttime blood pressure patterns and cardiovascular trends without directly measuring blood pressure. Access to health insights requires an Oura Membership at Rs 599 per month, a recurring cost that studio and gym operators should note when positioning wearable-linked programmes to members in the Indian market.
Source: News18 →
05
Precor launches selectorized line for its Glutebuilder range
Precor has expanded its Glutebuilder range with a new selectorized line, adding guided-movement machines that use weight stacks rather than plate loading. The machines were developed together with Glutebuilder and are designed to make targeted glute training accessible to members at different fitness levels. The move signals that equipment makers see dedicated glute training as a durable commercial category worth extending beyond specialist plate-loaded machines.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →

The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, will hold its 2026 annual event at the Hotel Meliá Costa del Sol in Torremolinos, near Málaga, Spain, from 20 to 23 October 2026, with tickets priced at €720 per participant. The programme includes expert talks, networking, and Les Mills workouts, with the opening reception hosted by DSSV chairman Prof. Dr. Thomas Wessinghage on 20 October. This is the first time the event leaves Mallorca, where the two previous editions were held.

DAILY
Tuesday, 27 October 2026 · Weekday
Whoop hits $10.1B valuation, Mark Mastrov enters HFA Hall of Fame & BODY20 targets women with strength focus
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Whoop reaches a $10.1 billion valuation, while BODY20 shifts its message toward strength and muscle preservation for women aged 35 and older.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Valuation
Whoop
 $10.1 billion
wearable fitness tracker company reaches $10.1 billion valuation
 
The rundown
01
Mark Mastrov to enter HFA Hall of Fame at March 2027 Las Vegas show
The Health & Fitness Association will induct 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov into its Hall of Fame on March 10 at The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Mastrov built 24 Hour Fitness from a single California gym into a global fitness company, then spent decades founding, investing in, and mentoring businesses across fitness, sports, and wellness. He recently returned as an owner of 24 Hour Fitness, more than 40 years after founding it.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
02
Whoop valued at $10.1 billion
Wearable fitness tracker company Whoop has reached a valuation of $10.1 billion.
Source: Fast Company →
03
Philip Donnay named GLL CEO as Peter Bundey retires
GLL has appointed Philip Donnay as CEO and Andy Bindon as deputy CEO. The appointments follow the retirement of Peter Bundey.
Source: Health Club Management →
04
BODY20 repositions its EMS model around strength training for women
BODY20, a 20-minute whole-body electrical muscle stimulation franchise, says it is targeting women seeking strength and muscle preservation rather than weight loss. About two-thirds of its members are women, most aged 35 to 55 or older, and director of fitness Sydney Maddox says member conversations have shifted away from calorie burning toward joint health, bone health and long-term capability. For studio operators, the trend suggests that marketing resistance training around longevity and muscle preservation, rather than weight loss, may better match what this demographic now wants.
Source: Athletech News →
05
Medo.check sets out eight factors for fitness studio software
German studio software provider medo.check has outlined eight principles for what it calls future-ready studio management software, published in trade magazine body Life. The principles cover customisation to individual studio workflows, system integration to avoid isolated data stores, a branded member app, and AI-assisted training monitoring through its medo.core product, while the company says its support line is staffed by people rather than automated tools. Medo.check positions the package around more than 20 years of experience in training management and member care, which may give studio operators a reference point when evaluating whether a software platform can handle both administration and coaching support in one system.
Source: body LIFE →
 
Stat
two-thirds
share of BODY20 members who are women
With roughly two-thirds of its member base being women, most aged 35 to 55 or older, BODY20's data gives studio operators a concrete indication of who is currently drawn to short-format electrical muscle stimulation sessions.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Monday, 26 October 2026
item.description: PureGym acquires Switzerland's NonStop Gym for £235 million, plus new data on member churn and a case for investing in general manager hiring.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 26 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 26 October 2026 · Weekday
PureGym buys NonStop Gym for £235m, Mariana Tek churn signals & Good Soul Hunting on GM hiring
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
PureGym acquires Switzerland's NonStop Gym for £235 million, plus new data on member churn and a case for investing in general manager hiring.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
PureGym / NonStop Gym
 £235 million
PureGym acquires 47-location Swiss low-cost chain NonStop Gym, deal expected to close 2 November 2026
 
Connect the dots
Member churn signals appear months before cancellation
Data from Mariana Tek, a studio management software platform, shows measurable changes in member behavior three to eight months before a cancellation or downgrade. Among members who eventually canceled, average monthly visits fell from 6.2 to 5.4 in the final month before cancellation, and monthly spend dropped 11%. Julie Sippy, director of marketing at Mariana Tek, said the membership change is often the end of a slow, subtle disengagement trajectory, not the beginning of one. The challenge for studios is that disengaging members may still attend classes and generate revenue, giving no obvious sign that they are at risk.
For studio operators, this means a member who looks active on a roster may already be drifting. Tracking visit frequency and spend trends over rolling months, rather than checking current membership status alone, gives studios a larger window to reach out and strengthen engagement before a cancellation decision is made.
 
The rundown
01
Mariana Tek: Member churn signals appear 3–8 months before cancellation
Data from Mariana Tek, a studio management software platform, shows measurable changes in member behavior three to eight months before a cancellation or downgrade. Among members who eventually canceled, average monthly visits fell from 6.2 to 5.4 in the final month before cancellation, and monthly spend dropped 11%. Studio operators who track visit frequency and spend trends over time may be able to identify at-risk members while there is still time to act.
Source: Athletech News →
02
PureGym buys Swiss chain NonStop Gym for £235 million
PureGym is acquiring NonStop Gym, a low-cost gym chain with 47 locations in Switzerland, for £235 million. The deal is expected to close on 2 November 2026, after which NonStop Gym sites will be rebranded as PureGym, giving the combined network more than 100 Swiss locations by end of 2026. The acquisition follows PureGym's purchase of Blink Fitness in the United States in 2024, and will make PureGym the largest low-cost gym operator in Switzerland.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Global Wellness Institute flags EMFs as an unaddressed factor in built environments
The Global Wellness Institute published an article stating that electromagnetic fields (EMFs) are present in almost every indoor space but are rarely considered in design decisions. Citing research from the Building Biology Institute, the article links elevated EMF exposure to changes in sleep, nervous system activity, cognitive fatigue, and melatonin regulation. Studio and gym operators who are already designing around light, air quality, and natural materials may find EMF exposure a relevant next consideration for their environments.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
04
J Potter Community Fitness raises £3,330 for Breast Cancer Now in one-week challenge
J Potter Community Fitness, based in Worcester, ran The Big Pink Journey from 14 to 21 October, with 100 supporters walking, dancing and exercising a combined 776 miles to raise £3,330 for Breast Cancer Now. The original targets were £1,500 and 315 miles. The campaign shows that a clearly defined distance goal and a one-week window can help small fitness communities significantly exceed fundraising targets.
Source: The Worcester News →
05
ViralSpoon joins DSSV as a supporting member
ViralSpoon, an AI social media management tool, has joined the DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, as a supporting member, announced on 21 October 2026. The tool connects to Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn and uses artificial intelligence to plan, create and publish posts automatically, matching a studio's existing visual style and tone. Studio operators running multiple locations can manage all accounts from a single dashboard, with campaigns adapted by the AI for each site so platforms do not flag them as duplicate content.
Source: DSSV →
06
Good Soul Hunting applies executive search methods to boutique fitness GM hiring
Good Soul Hunting, a fitness industry recruitment firm, is positioning the general manager role as a direct growth lever for boutique fitness operators. Co-founder and managing partner Matt Adey said a strong general manager or studio manager is responsible for turning a brand's vision into measurable results at the local level. For studio operators, the hire who runs the floor has more direct impact on member experience than any strategy set at head office.
Source: Athletech News →
 
Stat
3 to 8 months
how far in advance churn signals appear before a member cancels or downgrades, according to Mariana Tek data
Studios that monitor visit frequency and spend trends have a window of several months to identify at-risk members and act before a cancellation is made.

item.content:encoded:
Friday, 23 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Friday, 23 October 2026 · Weekday
Orangetheory adds Apple Watch tracking for $99, Club Studio plans two LA openings & JOHN REED launches in Stuttgart
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Orangetheory Fitness lets members connect their Apple Watch to its in-studio tracking platform for a one-time $99 fee, while Club Studio and JOHN REED each announce new locations.

The rundown
01
Orangetheory Fitness adds Apple Watch option for $99 one-time fee
Orangetheory Fitness launched OTconnect for Apple Watch on October 23 at participating U.S. studios, letting members pair their own Apple Watch to the brand's in-studio performance-tracking platform for a one-time $99 connection fee. During class, members can see heart rate, heart rate zones, calories burned and Splat Points on their wrist, and review a performance summary in the Orangetheory app afterward. The move shows one way a studio brand can offer members device choice while keeping proprietary tracking at the centre of the experience.
Source: Club Solutions →
02
Club Studio to open two new LA locations in Beverly Hills and Santa Monica
Club Studio, the premium group fitness concept from Fitness International, the parent company of LA Fitness, plans to open clubs at 8484 Wilshire Boulevard in Beverly Hills and 2001 Wilshire Boulevard in Santa Monica. The Santa Monica site will be its second in that city. No opening dates have been announced. The expansion shows continued appetite for concepts that combine boutique group fitness, strength and cardio equipment, personal training, and recovery services under one roof, a model studio owners in competitive urban markets may want to monitor.
Source: Athletech News →
03
Nirva raises $33m to launch AI pendant wearable
Nirva has raised $33 million to bring an AI pendant wearable to market.
Source: Traders Union →
04
JOHN REED opens first Stuttgart location at over 2,200 sq m
JOHN REED opened its first Fitness Music Club in Stuttgart, Germany, on 23 October 2026. The club, at Arnulf-Klett-Platz 1 near the main railway station, covers more than 2,200 square metres and includes cardio and strength equipment, a 110-square-metre functional training area, milon X machines, 12 Reformer Pilates benches from Your Reformer, planned regular HYROX classes, two saunas, a rest area, and a coffee and health bar.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
05
WILDE Raises $40M to Expand Protein Chip Range and Retail Reach
WILDE, a US maker of chips and crackers derived from chicken breast, egg whites, and bone broth, secured $40 million from investor S2G Investments on 22 October 2026 to expand retail distribution and launch new products. The company already sells in more than 30,000 retailers and recorded over $100 million in sales last year, and is opening a 130,000-square-foot facility that will increase production capacity sixfold. Coaches who sell or recommend snacks to clients may find high-protein whole-food options like these easier to position as consumer demand for protein-rich foods continues to grow.
Source: Fitt Insider →

retailers stocking WILDE protein chips and crackers
WILDE's presence in more than 30,000 retailers, combined with over $100 million in sales last year, shows that high-protein whole-food snacks have moved well beyond specialist health stores and into mainstream retail.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Thursday, 22 October 2026
item.description: Club Pilates is adding a circuit-style class and refreshing studios system-wide as it approaches 1500 locations, plus Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym sets a December opening.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 22 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Thursday, 22 October 2026 · Weekday
Club Pilates nears 1500 locations with new class format, Municipal Gym opens in December & HCM Invest launches in London
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Club Pilates is adding a circuit-style class and refreshing studios system-wide as it approaches 1500 locations, plus Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym sets a December opening.
Sqwod
 
Connect the dots
Club Pilates on growing to 1500 locations without losing what works
Tianna Strateman, brand president of Club Pilates, spoke with Club Solutions editor Taylor Gabhart on the Club Solutions podcast about how the brand is evolving as it approaches its 20th anniversary and 1500th location. The brand is introducing a circuit-style class format, driven by two signals Strateman identified: the rise of strength training and the growing use of GLP-1 medications. At the same time, Club Pilates is rolling out studio refreshes across its entire system, designed to limit disruption for franchisees and protect the member experience.
For studio owners, the approach offers a practical model: Strateman described how the brand chose which key performance indicators to track when launching changes across a large system, and how the physical updates were structured to keep return on investment clear for individual operators. The lesson is that innovation tied to measurable signals and tracked against specific metrics is easier to justify and manage than change for its own sake.
 
The rundown
01
Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym Set to Open in December
Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym is scheduled to open in December, with a focus on longevity, blood work and recovery. No further location or pricing details were confirmed in the source.
Source: Athletech News →
02
ACISO Consulting adds four staff across consulting, marketing and digital
ACISO Consulting, a fitness business consulting firm, has hired four people: Florian Otto as a consultant covering the Aachen region and German postcode area 5, Schirin Mameghani in online marketing, Nadya Ramzy as marketing manager, and Fabian Ackermann supporting digital processes. The hires were announced in October 2026. Studios working with ACISO can expect more regional coverage and expanded marketing support.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Club Pilates president explains push to 1500 locations and new class format
Tianna Strateman, brand president of Club Pilates, spoke with Club Solutions editor Taylor Gabhart on the Club Solutions podcast to discuss how the brand, approaching its 20th anniversary, is adding a circuit-style class format and rolling out studio refreshes across its system as it nears 1500 locations. Strateman said two industry signals, the rise of strength training and GLP-1 use, pointed the brand toward the new class offering. She also covered how the studio refreshes were designed to limit disruption for franchisees and which key performance indicators the brand tracks to measure a system-wide launch.
Source: Club Solutions →
04
HCM Invest launches in London on 21 October 2026
Health Club Management held the first HCM Invest event in London on 21 October 2026, bringing together investors, operators, entrepreneurs and advisers to explore investment and growth opportunities across fitness, health and wellness. Studio owners and coaches looking for funding or partnerships may find this kind of dedicated investor forum a useful channel to watch.
Source: Health Club Management →
05
Careerz Group launches AI coaching tool built on workforce assessment data
Careerz Group, based in Okemos, Michigan, announced Careerz Coach AI on October 20, 2026. The tool lets managers ask questions about people and workplace situations and receive guidance drawn from assessment data already collected through their workforce program, including DISC, JPTI, Motivators and emotional intelligence assessments. Coaches who use structured assessments with clients or staff may find this approach, connecting stored assessment results to real-time questions, a useful model for making assessment data more actionable day to day.
Source: markets.businessinsider.com →
06
Global Wellness Institute: Lack of Belonging Is a Major Driver of Workplace Stress
The Global Wellness Institute has published a piece arguing that workplace culture, not standalone programs, is the foundation of employee mental wellbeing. It identifies lack of belonging as a large cause of workplace stress, alongside pressure from leaders, self-imposed overwork, and exclusion by colleagues. For coaches and studio owners who employ staff, the piece suggests that culture built by leaders matters more than any single wellness offering.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
 
Stat
1500
Club Pilates locations as the brand approaches its 20th anniversary
The scale shows how far a single modality can travel when it is franchised consistently, and sets the context for why system-wide launches require careful measurement.

item.title: Sqwod Daily · Wednesday, 21 October 2026
item.description: The ACSM has ranked wearable technology as the world's top fitness trend for 2027, while Fitness On Demand expands its digital library and Unravel Health secures new funding.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 · Weekday
ACSM names wearable tech top fitness trend for 2027, Fitness On Demand adds 99 Mvmnt workouts & Unravel Health raises €2.5M
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
The ACSM has ranked wearable technology as the world's top fitness trend for 2027, while Fitness On Demand expands its digital library and Unravel Health secures new funding.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Unravel Health
 €2.5M
raised to launch the Micro Lab, an at-home saliva-based hormone testing device shipping in 2027
 
Connect the dots
ACSM ranks wearable technology the top global fitness trend for 2027
The American College of Sports Medicine published its 21st annual fitness trend survey on 21 October 2026. More than 1,400 fitness professionals rated 50 potential trends. Wearable technology came first, followed by mobile fitness apps and balance, flow and core training. The ACSM releases this ranking each year to show which services and tools are drawing the most attention across the industry internationally.
For coaches and studio owners, the top-ten list is a practical reference point. If wearables and mobile apps are leading globally, clients are likely already tracking their own data. Knowing the ranking helps you decide which tools and services to prioritise or promote in the coming year.
 
The rundown
01
ACSM names wearable technology the top global fitness trend for 2027
The American College of Sports Medicine published its 21st annual fitness trend survey on 21 October 2026. More than 1,400 fitness professionals rated 50 potential trends, placing wearable technology first, followed by mobile fitness apps and balance, flow and core training. Coaches and studio owners can use the top-ten ranking to judge which services and tools are drawing the most attention internationally.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
02
Fitness On Demand adds 99 Mvmnt workouts to its digital library
Fitness On Demand, a commercial fitness platform serving studios, gyms and wellness operators, announced a content partnership with Mvmnt, a digital fitness platform, on 14 October 2026 in Minneapolis. The deal adds 99 Mvmnt workouts covering strength, cardio, boxing, dance, yoga, Pilates, mobility and meditation to Fitness On Demand's existing library of more than 1,800 workouts, available across in-facility screens and mobile touchpoints. Studio and gym owners can broaden their programming offer without hiring more instructors or adding a separate app.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
03
ØRA Wellness Studio raises over €1,000 for Breast Cancer Awareness
ØRA Wellness Studio in Athlone, Ireland, raised over €1,000 at its Pink Wellness Morning, organised by studio owner Aishling Croughan and life coach Libby Hayes. The event brought women together for gentle movement, breathwork, coffee and cake, with support from local businesses including Mary's SuperValu Athlone, A Room in Bloom and Sláinte Coffee Shop. The event shows how studios can partner with local businesses and community figures to run charity events that build connection and generate goodwill.
Source: Westmeath Independent →
04
Unravel Health Raises €2.5M for At-Home Hormone Testing Device
Women's hormone monitoring company Unravel Health has raised €2.5 million to launch the Micro Lab, an at-home device that reads estradiol and other biomarkers from saliva in minutes. The device ships in 2027, with plans to add more hormones and expand into men's health. Coaches who work with clients on hormonal health, such as perimenopause or cycle-based training, may eventually have access to daily, lab-grade data rather than relying on single blood test snapshots.
Source: Fitt Insider →
 
Stat
1,800
workouts in Fitness On Demand's library before the Mvmnt partnership
Fitness On Demand already held more than 1,800 workouts; the addition of 99 Mvmnt sessions covering strength, cardio, boxing, dance, yoga, Pilates, mobility and meditation gives operators a broader programming range without adding equipment or staff.

Source: Irish Legal News →
02
Alexander Sosa opens his 20th Sports Club with €5m investment in Hamburg
Entrepreneur Alexander Sosa opened his 20th Sports Club location in Hamburg-Poppenbüttel in October 2026, celebrating with around 400 guests. The new 5,000-square-metre fitness and wellness facility was converted from a former electronics store at a cost of around five million euros. The project shows that large-scale conversion of retail space into fitness facilities remains a viable route for operators looking to expand in established urban areas.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Jazzercise Founder Judi Sheppard Missett to Enter HFA Hall of Fame in 2027
The Health & Fitness Association will induct Judi Sheppard Missett, founder and executive chair of Jazzercise, into its Hall of Fame on March 10, 2027, during the opening night of The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Missett built Jazzercise from a class of 15 women into a global dance fitness company over more than five decades. HFA Interim President and CEO Greta Wagner said Missett changed how millions of people experience fitness and created entrepreneurship opportunities for generations of women.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
04
RockSalt Pilates Hires Franchise Veteran as COO With 84 Locations in Development
Music-driven Pilates brand RockSalt Pilates has appointed Stephanie Knepp, a franchise veteran, as its new chief operating officer. The brand has 84 locations in development, including sites in the UAE. Studio owners considering franchise growth can watch how an experienced franchise operator shapes a scaled rollout at a boutique concept.
Source: Athletech News →

Having 84 sites in development, including locations in the UAE, shows how quickly a boutique Pilates brand can scale through franchising once it brings in experienced operational leadership.

item.description: Today: an Amsterdam startup raises €1 million to replace patchwork gym software, a Canadian Lagree brand heads to California, and a German briefing on insurer-funded courses.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 19 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
Monday, 19 October 2026 · Weekday
Huppa raises €1M for studio software, Reformd plans a US Lagree flagship & DSSV prevention courses
Your edge in the fitness industry. Five minutes, every weekday.
Today: an Amsterdam startup raises €1 million to replace patchwork gym software, a Canadian Lagree brand heads to California, and a German briefing on insurer-funded courses.
Sqwod
 
Money movement
▲  Raise
Huppa
 €1M
pre-seed round for an all-in-one platform for gyms, CrossFit boxes and studios
 
Connect the dots
Huppa wants to replace the patchwork of studio software
Huppa, an Amsterdam startup founded in 2024 by two gym owners, has raised €1 million in pre-seed funding. Its platform combines member management, class scheduling, payments, financial reporting and automation in one system, connects to Mollie, Urban Sports Club and ClassPass, and charges by the number of active customers. The founders say many gyms and studios still run on outdated software, spend too much time on admin and miss chances to grow revenue because their data is spread across tools.
For a studio owner, the takeaway is practical: every separate tool you pay for is another login, another export and another place where member data can go missing. Whether or not you look at Huppa, it is worth knowing exactly how many systems your business runs on and what they cost together.
 
The rundown
01
Huppa raises €1M to build one platform for running a gym
Amsterdam startup Huppa has raised €1 million in pre-seed funding for software that combines member management, scheduling, payments and reporting for gyms, CrossFit boxes and studios. It was founded in 2024 by two gym owners and charges by the number of active customers.
Source: EU-Startups →
02
Reformd plans the world's largest Lagree studio in California
Toronto's Reformd, owned by Sweat and Tonic, will open a studio in Calabasas in January 2027 with 37 Lagree machines and six recovery rooms. The recovery services, including cryotherapy and compression therapy, will be open to people who do not take classes.
Source: Athletech News →
03
DSSV briefing on insurer-funded prevention courses, 19 November
Germany's fitness operators' association, the DSSV, is holding an online briefing on 19 November on its courses Kraft Aktiv and Cardio-Fitness. Both are free for members and certified so German studios can bill them to health insurers.
Source: DSSV →

The DSSV is holding an online briefing on 19 November (12:30 to 13:30) on its prevention courses Kraft Aktiv and Cardio-Fitness. Both are free for DSSV members and certified so studios can bill them to German health insurers.
